title: Stability pilot cadence blueprint — cross-team SLO rollout (Q2 2026)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working blueprint for a 6-week cross-team pilot to operationalize SLOs and an ops cadence across three representative services (ingest-api, generation-worker, embedding-cache). The goal is to validate a repeatable pattern for: defining SLIs/SLOs, wiring telemetry/dashboards, running an initial error-budget policy, and exercising escalation/fallback playbooks.

Why this pilot (context):
- We need a minimal, repeatable path to ship SLOs that teams can adopt without heavy bespoke work.
- Prior docs focus on governance and long-term rollout; this is tactical: how teams actually do it in sprints.
- Focus on pairing a product/feature service (ingest-api), a real-time model-inference path (generation-worker), and a caching infra component (embedding-cache) to capture different failure modes.

High-level timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): stakeholder kickoff, service selection, access checks, instrumentation audit.
- Sprint A (Weeks 1–2): discovery & SLI design.
- Sprint B (Weeks 3–4): telemetry, dashboards, alerts, basic automation.
- Sprint C (Weeks 5–6): error budget policy, canary/rollout simulation, retro + adoption plan.

Cadence and meetings (minimal overhead):
- Weekly pilot sync (30m): cross-team leads; agenda: blockers, next steps, metric review.
- Core squad standup (Mon/Wed/Fri 15m): SRE + one service owner + observability engineer.
- Bi-weekly exec readout (30m every 2 weeks): product and infra leadership.
- Ad-hoc war room during smoke tests or simulated incidents.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Pilot Lead (Marcus Lee): overall coordination, deadlines, vendor/infra requests.
- SRE Lead (Aisha Patel): validates SLIs, sets alerts, owns error budget automation.
- Observability Engineer (Rina Kaur): dashboard + instrumentation changes, metric tagging.
- Service Owners (Diego Alvarez — ingest-api; Liam O'Connor — generation-worker; Priya Shah — embedding-cache): decide acceptable SLO targets, run canary simulations, implement minor service-side telemetry hooks.
- Product Representative: clarifies customer-impact thresholds and priority features.

Minimum deliverables per service by end of pilot:
1) SLI definitions (documented): at least one availability and one latency SLI with precise sampling/query method.
2) SLO targets: quantifiable target and review window (30d rolling, 7d burn check, p95 latency thresholds).
3) Dashboards: service-level dashboard with SLI time series, error budget consumption, and request volume.
4) Alerts: two classes — (a) early-warning (error-budget burn > 25% in 24h), (b) incident (error-budget exhausted).
5) Runbook snippet: immediate mitigation steps + owner contact.
6) Automated burn policy: a simple PagerDuty integration that notifies SRE when the 25% trigger fires.

Suggested SLI candidates (examples):
- ingest-api: success-rate (2xx/total) sampled at request level; p95 end-to-end for POST /upload.
- generation-worker: p95 generation latency (model start->last token), and per-request error boolean (modelOOM/timeout).
- embedding-cache: cache hit-rate by request category; miss latency p95.

Proposed SLOs (pilot defaults — teams can opt-out/change):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% over 30d for ingest-api (request success-rate).
- Latency SLO: generation-worker p95 < 350ms over 30d.
- Cache effectiveness SLO: embedding-cache hit-rate >= 92% over 30d.
Notes: targets are intentionally aggressive for pilot — part of validation is feasibility.

Sprint-level tasks (detailed):
- Sprint A (Discovery & SLI design):
  * Run instrumentation audit (logs, traces, metrics) — Rina.
  * Identify queryable metrics and missing tags/labels — SRE + service owners.
  * Draft SLI math and test queries in metrics backend (PromQL/SQL).
  * Define acceptable SLO window, burn-rate policy, and initial targets.
  * Jira tickets: create per-service SLO epic, link to pilot coordination ticket (ENGSRE-4821).

- Sprint B (Telemetry + dashboards):
  * Implement missing instrumentation: attach request-id tags, add error classification counters.
  * Build dashboards: time-series, burn counters, traffic-normalized views.
  * Create alert rules: low-noise thresholds for pilot.
  * Smoke test the alert pipeline (send test signals).

- Sprint C (Policy + exercise):
  * Wire a simple error-budget automation: create PD escalation for >25% burn in 24h.
  * Run a controlled canary or traffic shift to simulate partial outage and observe burn.
  * Execute an incident playbook run and note gaps (timing, ownership confusion).
  * Retro: capture findings and produce an adoption guide for other teams.

Success criteria (what 'good' looks like):
- All three services have documented SLIs + SLOs and dashboards that are used during at least one simulated incident.
- Alert noise < 2 false positives during pilot (goal).
- Error-budget automation triggers correctly in simulation and escalates to SRE.
- Clear adoption checklist for other teams with < 4 hours of onboarding work estimated.

Risks and mitigations:
- Metric fidelity risk: missing tags or high-cardinality labels make queries slow. Mitigation: observational audit first; prefer aggregated counters with a cardinality plan.
- Alert fatigue: too-sensitive alerts swamp teams. Mitigation: start conservative; use burn-based early warning not immediate paging.
- Cross-team dependency on infra changes (e.g., logging agent upgrade). Mitigation: get infra sign-off during Week 0 and block non-critical infra changes during pilot windows.
- Data retention limits: our metrics retention might truncate 30d windows. Mitigation: use downsampled rollups and store SLO rollup series.

Communication plan:
- Weekly pilot note posted to #sre-pilot Slack with short bullets and links to dashboards.
- End-of-sprint email to infra/product leadership summarizing progress and asks.
- Confluence page (linked_artifacts above) for final deliverables and onboarding how-to.

Checklist before kickoff (Week 0):
- [ ] Confirm service owners and core squad.
- [ ] Grant metric/storage access for Rina + SRE.
- [ ] Baseline telemetry audit submitted.
- [ ] Create project Jira epics and invite reviewers.
- [ ] Reserve a short block on exec calendar for two bi-weekly readouts.

Open questions / notes-to-self (to resolve in Week 0):
- Can product sign off on 30d rolling window for all three services? Some features prefer 7d.
- Is 25% burn threshold the right early-warning level for customer-facing endpoints?
- Confirm retention for raw request traces — we may need to extend for debugging.
- Evaluate whether we should use "volume-normalized" burn (e.g., burn per thousand requests) for low-traffic services.

Artifacts to generate during pilot (deliverables):
- Per-service SLI spec (one-pager).
- Dashboards + share links.
- Alert rule definitions (as code where possible).
- Runbook snippets and incident notes.
- Pilot retro doc and adoption checklist.

Next steps (immediate):
- Kickoff meeting: 2026-04-12 10:00 PT (invite sent).
- Assign Jira tickets and label with pilot:pilot-q2-2026.
- Rina to run initial instrumentation audit by 2026-04-16.

If you're reading this and want to join the pilot or suggest a service candidate, ping me (Marcus) on Slack.

-- end blueprint --
